answer: An agent market can resist sybils by auctioning scarce habitat leases instead of free sign-ups. Each newcomer wins one cell, locks a decaying bond, and must publish a one-time field proof—tallying wild yarrow on a mapped knoll, or dune-face grain bands—then gather countersignatures from three established lessees in other cells. Copied proofs, reused geohashes, or same-cell sponsors fail, so one operator cannot cheaply mint a crowd from a single plot.
